title: Newbigin's return
hookLine: a missionary to India returns to Britain and sees the West as a mission field too

lines: THE WEST IS A MISSION FIELD TOO.
cards: A young minister sits in South India, saying Tamil words aloud until they stick. He has sailed out from Britain as a missionary of the Church of Scotland, and he stays for years.
He preaches in villages, and becomes a bishop in the Church of South India. Then, near the end of his working life, he comes home to Britain. And home looks strange to him.
Thinner congregations. A culture that once called itself Christian, now living by other stories. Lesslie Newbigin looked hard at his own country and said it plainly: the West is a mission field too.

teach.b: A missionary has to learn to see a culture from outside: what its people take for granted, what stories they live by, what they'd never think to question. Newbigin had done that for years in India.
Back in Britain, he turned the same eyes on his own culture.

teach.h: THE WEST HAS ITS OWN STORIES.
teach.b: He saw that the modern West had its own unquestioned beliefs, like any culture, and he thought Christians there had made too much peace with them without noticing.
So he asked the missionary's question at home: how does the gospel sound here, to these neighbors? His answer had a surprising focus.

Not mainly big campaigns: the local congregation. A congregation actually living the gospel, he wrote, in its worship, its care for neighbors and its life together, is how people come to understand the gospel at all.
In John's Gospel, the risen Jesus says to his disciples: "as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you." Newbigin drew no line there between those who go far away and those who stay.
For him, every disciple is sent, and home is where the sending starts.

This week has walked through a house of many rooms: Rahner's ordinary, Schmemann's sacrament, Gutiérrez from below, Cone's cross, women's voices, Pentecostal power. And Newbigin, seeing his own front door with fresh eyes.

how: Some congregations speak of their own neighborhood as their mission field, through hospitality, local service and simply being present; Newbigin's books are read by church leaders across traditions.

games.q: you've spent years as a missionary abroad. now you've come home to a country that once called itself Christian. what do you do?
o: look at home the way a missionary would.
move abroad again as soon as possible.
games.why: Newbigin turned a missionary's eyes on his own culture and asked how the gospel sounds there, pointing to the local congregation.

practice: Picture the street where you live, and look at it the way a newcomer would, someone just arrived from far away: what do people here take for granted, what do they hope for and fear, and who is lonely? Don't judge it; just look.
If you pray, you can hold your neighbors before God, one doorway at a time.

wordCard.voice: Newbigin's return. Lesslie Newbigin, home from India, seeing his own country as a mission field, and the local church as the place the gospel is explained by being lived.
